summary.headline: Marksans FY26 revenue rose 12.5% to INR2,951 crores with record PAT of INR420 crores; Q4 EBITDA margin hit 22.8%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue grew 20.8% YoY to INR856 crores, with all three major regions growing and UK/EU posting its highest-ever quarter at INR308 crores. Q4 EBITDA rose 54% to INR195 crores, with margin up 491 bps to 22.8%, helped by mix, operating leverage and softer raw material costs in H2. Management flagged raw material inflation of 20-30% on petroleum-linked inputs for Q1 FY27, though it said inventory covers Q1 to a large extent. The company remains debt free with INR990 crores cash, a final dividend of INR0.90 per share was recommended, and FY27 guidance is 15-20% revenue growth with EBITDA margin in the 20-21% range.

financial_highlights.change: Cash from operations INR458 crores; capex INR131 crores

financial_highlights.value: INR0.90 per share (90% of face value)

segments.name: North America (US)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,533 crores, up 24%, now 52% of total; Q4 INR406 crores. Company launched 112 SKUs in FY26 with 51 more in pipeline; Teva-acquired facility at close to 50% utilisation with 40-50% further growth cited.

segments.name: UK and EU
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR308 crores (record, +12.3% YoY) after pricing pressure earlier in FY26; FY26 INR1,015 crores. Company has 18 new product approvals, 30 under review, 24 awaiting approval, and plans over 200 UK filings over 4 years.

segments.name: Australia and New Zealand
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR123 crores (+61.3% YoY); FY26 INR303 crores. Nova Pharma entered prescription generics with 11 branded generic launches; management says about halfway to a USD100 million target within 3 years.

segments.name: Rest of world / new markets
segments.commentary: Rest of world revenue INR19 crores in Q4 and INR99 crores in FY26. Germany entered organically; Canada products under filing with approvals expected late FY27; Europe revenue contribution expected in H2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided conservatively at 15-20% YoY.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected to stay in the 20-21% range, per management, despite raw material inflation.
Target of INR4,000 crores revenue within about 2 years (by FY28) reiterated; roadmap to double revenue in 3-5 years.
Raw material costs expected to rise in Q1 FY27 due to petroleum-linked input inflation of 20-30%; inventory covers Q1 to a great extent.
Management expects M&A activity in 2027; one target in due diligence, another not yet started. Europe revenue contribution expected in H2 FY27.
Quarterly seasonality: Q1 typically lowest, Q3 peak; management declined to treat Q4 FY26 as an FY27 run rate.
capex_capacity: Total capacity of about 26 billion units across three facilities; operational capacity currently about 13-14 billion units, roughly 50-55% utilisation.
Teva facility (Goa, about 8 billion units) at close to 50% utilisation; some capex planned within the facility for new dosage forms.
FY26 capex INR131 crores, mainly for the new facility and maintenance; management says major capex cycle is complete.
No land bank outside Goa at present; management says it is evaluating land banks or acquiring plants for future capacity expansion.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices up 20-30% on petroleum-linked inputs and intermediates; inventory of 5-6 months on key raw materials per management.
Customer contract renegotiation held back for now; management is waiting for clarity, citing force majeure as a possible route if conflict prolongs.
Logistics costs about 2% margin impact, similar to the Red Sea period, but management said freight impact is much lower than Red Sea.
US market described as very competitive with pricing pressure; Europe and UK seen as relatively better on margin.
Forex movement partly offsets raw material cost rise as export revenues are USD-linked.

qa_highlights.question: How will raw material inflation flow through margins and customer contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 20-30% price rises on petroleum-linked raw materials, with inventory covering Q1 to a great extent. It said contract renegotiation is possible but the company is waiting for clarity.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY28 INR4,000 crores revenue target still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management said INR4,000 crores within the next 2 years is very much on the plate, with a roadmap to double revenue in 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Can Q4 be used as an FY27 run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined; it said Q1 is seasonally lowest and Q3 the peak, and that the company should be judged on a year-on-year basis.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 margin and growth expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA margin expected to stay the same (20-21% range); revenue growth guided conservatively at 15-20%.

qa_highlights.question: What are plans for the INR990 crore cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is optimistic on M&A in 2027: one target is in due diligence and another has not started. Targets could be in any geography or platform, with a conservative valuation focus.

qa_highlights.question: When will new markets (Canada, Europe) contribute revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Canada approvals expected late FY27 with small revenue; Europe expected to contribute in H2 FY27, earlier than planned.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation of 20-30% in Q1 FY27 if the geopolitical disruption persists; inventory cover may run down.
Working capital at 138 days, elevated after building inventory during the tariff period; management wants to go lighter over time.
US pricing pressure and tariff uncertainty.
Timing of Teva facility utilisation gains and new product approvals, which take about a year.
Execution on M&A deployment of the INR990 crore cash balance; management's timeline is 2027.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, margins and the balance sheet, but noticeably cautious on raw material pricing and customer renegotiation, where management repeatedly said it is waiting for clarity. Answers on M&A and new market timing were forward-looking without firm numbers.
key_quotes: So yes, I mean, INR4,000 crores within the next 2 years is very much on the plate right now.
I mean conservatively because I always like to be that way but between 15% to 20%.
We closed FY26 with a cash and cash equivalent of approximately INR990 crores.

adds.what: Total capacity about 26 billion units across three facilities; operational capacity ~13-14 billion units (existing, not new additions)
Some capex planned within the Goa Teva facility for new dosage forms (amount not stated)

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% (midpoint 17.5%) with EBITDA margin held at 20-21%, backed by 112 FY26 SKU launches with 51 in pipeline, 18 UK/EU approvals plus 30 under review, and Nova's 11 branded generic launches; capacity is ample (utilisation ~52%, Teva Goa facility near 50%), but no new capacity addition has a stated timeline and raw material inflation of 20-30% is a headwind.
